what_it_measured.text: Methods: Two candidate miniproteins, a homotrimeric construct (Trimer, IPD-52520, 17 kDa) and a tandem fusion construct (Daisy, IPD-52521, 25 kDa), were evaluated in parallel through systematic optimization of strain selection, media formulation, fed-batch fermentation, inclusion-body solubilization, refolding, and chromatographic purification.
Endotoxin was quantified by a kinetic chromogenic LAL assay (EU/mg protein). 2.6.

dose.text: Endotoxin Removal PEI at 0.05% achieved effective endotoxin reduction while preserving protein recovery; concentrations ≥ 0.1% caused approximately 50% yield loss.

endpoint.text: Methods: Two candidate miniproteins, a homotrimeric construct (Trimer, IPD-52520, 17 kDa) and a tandem fusion construct (Daisy, IPD-52521, 25 kDa), were evaluated in parallel through systematic optimization of strain selection, media formulation, fed-batch fermentation, inclusion-body solubilization, refolding, and chromatographic purification.
Purity and molecular weight were assessed by SDS-PAGE (gradient gels) and SEC-HPLC.
Endotoxin was quantified by a kinetic chromogenic LAL assay (EU/mg protein). 2.6.

reported_results.text: UF/DF with 30 kDa MWCO membranes increased purity from approximately 75–85% to >90%, primarily by removing Low-Molecular-Weight (LMW) species.
Subsequent treatment with an endotoxin-removal resin reduced levels from 160–210 EU/mg to 20–30 EU/mg (86–88% removal efficiency). 3.7.
Endotoxin Removal PEI at 0.05% achieved effective endotoxin reduction while preserving protein recovery; concentrations ≥ 0.1% caused approximately 50% yield loss.
A transient HMW increase at 3 months (4%, reverting to 1% at 6 months) may reflect assay variability rather than a true aggregation event.
The temporary increase in HMW under accelerated stress (4% at 3 months, returning to 1% at 6 months) appears to be due to assay variability rather than true aggregation.
